html:
The wars from 1803 to 1815 between Napoleon's France and shifting coalitions of European powers led by Britain. They followed the wars of the French Revolution and redrew the map of Europe and beyond.

  • 1805: the British navy under Nelson destroyed the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar, and Napoleon crushed Austria and Russia at Austerlitz.
  • 1806: the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved. Napoleon banned trade with Britain across Europe, the Continental System.
  • 1807: Britain bombarded Copenhagen and took the fleet of Denmark-Norway, using rockets copied from the Mysorean rockets fired at British troops in India.
  • 1808 to 1814: war in Spain and Portugal. The Portuguese court fled to Brazil, and the collapse of Spanish rule at home set off the Spanish American wars of independence.
  • 1812: Napoleon invaded Russia and lost most of his army.
  • 1814 to 1815: he was beaten, exiled to Elba, returned, and was finally defeated at the Battle of Waterloo.

The war reached the colonies too: Britain took Dutch Java, which Stamford Raffles governed from 1811. Denmark lost Norway to Sweden in 1814. The Congress of Vienna then set the borders of Europe for a generation. French law spread through the Napoleonic Code. Jane Austen wrote her novels in these years, with the navy and the militia in the background.
sum: The wars from 1803 to 1815 between Napoleon's France and shifting coalitions of European powers led by Britain. They followed the wars of the French Revolution and redrew the map of Europe and beyond.
